To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
uniform frequency images can be created by warping arbitrary images and that the resulting warped, downsample images have superior quality when compared to images downsampled without the warping.

(i) the frequency properties of images can be manipulated to achieve space-efficient textures; (ii) this manipulation can be done automatically; and (iii) the original image can be reconstructed during rendering by applying a warping function and rendering the image as a texture map.

1) we introduce the notion of uniform frequency images; 2) we present a general algorithm to automatically generate warping functions to produce uniform frequency images; and 3) we present an efficient implementation of this warping algorithm that can be used for image compression and texture mapping.
